embeds.title: 🟡 GM Agrees to $12.75M California Settlement Over Sale of Drivers' Data
embeds.description:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced a $12.75 million settlement with General Motors over allegations that the company violated the California Consumer Privacy Act by illegally collecting and selling Californians' driving and location data to data brokers Verisk Analytics and LexisNexis Risk Solutions between 2020 and 2024. The data was collected through GM's OnStar subsidiary and 'Smart Driver' system for driver-scoring products related to insurance. GM is required to stop selling driving data for five years, delete retained data within 180 days unless consumers consent, and implement stronger privacy compliance programs.

embeds.title: 🔴 ShinyHunters Claims Data Theft from Instructure Canvas, Threatens Extortion
embeds.description:
**Actor:** ShinyHunters
ShinyHunters, affiliated with The Com, claims responsibility for a cyberattack on Instructure's Canvas learning management platform and threatens to leak 3.65 terabytes of data spanning 275 million records across 8,809 school systems unless ransom is paid. The threat group defaced Canvas login pages at roughly 330 institutions and set extortion deadlines. Instructure CEO Steve Daly acknowledged the attack exposed usernames, email addresses, course names, enrollment information and messages, but stated course content, submissions and credentials were not compromised. The incident prompted Canvas to go offline, disrupting schools nationwide, and drew attention from the House Homeland Security Committee.
**Sources:** CyberScoop • 🟡 2 corroborating
**CVEs:** none • **Access:** Free-For-Teacher account vulnerability exploitation
**Incident date:** 2026-04-29 • **Confidence:** claim
